messages.author: 32bf4f27a31a68db
messages.subject: Conditional Ordered Logistic Regression
parts:
HI,

Does anybody have any experience building a model with Conditional Ordered Logistic Regression?

In the past, I've build Stan models with Conditional Logistic Regression by directly adding the derivative of the likelihood to the target value.  You can see in the dummy code below how I iterate over each group and update the target value.

model {
  vector[N] mu;        
  int pos;
  
  b ~ normal(0, 1);
  
  mu = x * b;

  pos = 1;
  for (ii in 1:n_grp) { // log likelihood is a sum over each group
    vector[obs_per_grp[ii]] mu_g;
  
    mu_g = segment(mu, pos, obs_per_grp[ii]);
    target += (mu_g[1] - log_sum_exp(mu_g));
    
    pos = pos + obs_per_grp[ii];
}

This has worked nicely.

Now, I want to try something similar but with Ordered Logistic Regression.  The Stan manual describes the function of ordered_logistic(), but that won't take into account the conditional part of the model.

Any thoughts or suggestions?

Thanks!

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Conditional Ordered Logistic Regression
parts:
I read the Wikipedia page on conditional ordered logistic
regression. Is that the one you're using?

1. I don't see where derivatives come in.

2. The problem it's trying to solve for MLE isn't a problem
for a Bayesian hierarchical model.

3. Your

> mu_g = segment(mu, pos, obs_per_grp[ii]);
> target += (mu_g[1] - log_sum_exp(mu_g));

is equivalent to

1 ~ categorical_logit(mu[pos:pos + obs_per_grp[ii]]);

so I don't see where all the conditional stuff comes in.
But if that's all you're trying to do, you might be able
to do the same thing with the built in ordinal logit.

- Bob
